text:
emma: FYI customer AcmeAnalytics reporting massive 429s + high tail latency after we pushed the new rate policy canary to their org at 09:12 UTC. Ticket #CA-9274.

jordan: tagging — I was on the rollout. Which canary group was that?

emma: they were in canary-group-7 (10% orgs) — policy v3.0 with burst_cap=200, steady_rate=50r/s, smoothing=off.

ryan: copy. Do we have their request profile? heavy long-running embedding jobs?

emma: yes they run async batch embeddings every 5m, bursts ~1200 concurrent small requests for 60s windows. Before rollout they were fine. After, we see 429 + many auth failures intermittently.

claudia: auth failures? that's odd, rate policy shouldn't touch auth. Any 401s in the logs?

emma: logs show both 429 responses and intermittent 401: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":30}
```
and occasionally:
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid_api_key","code":"billing_suspended"}
```

sam: billing_suspended? That sounds like a separate billing flag flipped for that tenant. Could be race with quota enforcement.

jordan: pulling traces. prometheus quick queries: 
```
sum(rate(api_requests_total{org="AcmeAnalytics"}[1m])) by (status)
http_requests_total{org="AcmeAnalytics",status="429"}[5m]
```
I see a spike in 429s at 09:12 matching rollout. Latency p95 for /v1/embeddings jumped from 1.1s -> 3.6s. Queue length on inference workers increased ~x4.

ryan: sounds like burst smoothing off allowed immediate burst to saturate per-worker token budget; then we triggered rate cap which returned 429s; meanwhile billing service retried calls to auth and hit a soft limit causing intermittent billing_suspended responses that look like 401s. Two independent backpressure signals.

emma: customer says they see client-side retries that pile up and then auth errors start appearing. They lost visibility since they rely on consistent retry-after headers.

claudia: can we repro quickly? I have a small script to simulate their profile.

sam: share curl snippet so support can repro locally.

emma: here's a repro we ran from stage (replaced keys):
```
for i in {1..400}; do 
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test-ACME" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"input":"short text"}' &
done; wait
```
Expected: many 429s and a few 401s when billing svc skews.

jordan: thanks. I also saw the canary rollout script changed the smoothing flag inadvertently (it defaulted to off for v3). We intended smoothing=leaky_alpha=0.2 to smooth spikes.

ryan: action plan suggestion: 1) pause the canary rollout for group-7 immediately, 2) trigger a rollback to v2 for that group, 3) whitelist Acme temporarily to avoid billing auto-suspend while we diagnose, 4) add smoothing param and re-run a controlled canary with telemetry.

claudia: +1. How do we pause? ops-bot?

ops-bot: @jordan executed: rollback_policy --org-group canary-group-7 --target v2 --reason "support escal: Acme 429s" --now
ops-bot: rollback job started (job-id: rb-20240613-91). Estimated finish 45s.

emma: rollback in progress. I've messaged the customer that we're rolling back and asked for their retry settings (backoff).

sam: I'll coordinate with billing team to temporarily remove auto-suspend for Acme org while we stabilize. Opening billing incident BL-410.

jordan: after rollback we should verify health: check 429 counts, auth 401s, p95 latency, inference queue depth for last 10m. Prometheus queries I recommend:
```
increase(http_requests_total{org="AcmeAnalytics",status="429"}[5m])
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/embeddings",org="AcmeAnalytics"}[5m])) by (le))
avg(inference_queue_length{pool="shared"}[2m])
```

ryan: also add a temporary rule in routing to limit client retry concurrency for that org to 100 concurrent requests to avoid thundering herd while we repopulate caches. That'll be a short-lived mitigation.

claudia: I'll schedule the re-canary but with smoothing enabled and a lower burst_cap=100 and injected client-retry-rate-limit. We should run a synthetic test first.

emma: customer confirmed they saw fewer 429s after rollback started. They still have some in-flight failures but overall better.

ops-bot: rollback job rb-20240613-91 completed successfully.

jordan: verified: 429s dropped by 88% for Acme in the 5m after rollback; p95 latency back to ~1.2s. Billing team: any change to the billing_suspended spike?

sam: billing team rolled back a temporary enforcement rule that was applied to orgs exceeding nightly spend delta; it was catching some async retries as fraud and flipping suspend flag. That hang removed now.

ryan: root causes summary: (A) policy v3 defaulted smoothing=off which allowed sudden bursts to exhaust worker-level budgets; (B) a concurrent billing enforcement rule was over-eager and produced 401s under retry load; (C) client retry settings amplified both effects.

claudia: next steps: 1) patch rollout script to require explicit smoothing param (no implicit off), 2) add canary preflight synthetic that simulates large short bursts for batch customers, 3) add an observable to correlate billing suspend events with request bursts, 4) docs note about recommended client retry concurrency/backoff for batch workloads.

emma: I'll follow up with Acme with a timeline and ask for their retry/backoff config; ask them to throttle to 100 concurrent for now.

jordan: thanks everyone. I'll open a postmortem ticket and tag eng-platform and billing. Assigning followups: jordan (patch rollout script), claudia (re-canary plan), sam (billing rule rollback review), ryan (routing temporary rate-limit), emma (customer comms).

emma: thanks team :thumbsup:

ryan: nice coordination. logging action items in #incidents for formal postmortem.

ops-bot: Created incident INC-20240613-77 and linked thread.
